# cashew test fixtures

Two families. **Tests never invoke gpg or the network — they read these committed bytes.**

## `real/` — the deterministic, toolchain-pinned anchors

The actual kernel.org signer keys + a real release signature, the ground truth that the whole design
rests on. Provenance + every asserted fact is in `real/METADATA.toml`.

- `greg-pruned.asc`, `sasha-pruned.asc` — Greg Kroah-Hartman + Sasha Levin public keys, exported
  through the **§5.0 vendoring command** (pruned, minimized, attribute-free, armored) from the
  **authoritative `pgpkeys.git`** at commit `ebb799f8`, toolchain **gpg 2.4.9 / libgcrypt 1.12.2**.
- `linux-6.6.30.tar.sign` — a real detached release signature (fetched from cdn.kernel.org). Its
  hashed issuer fingerprint is Greg's **primary** (the operative kernel.org shape).

**Key material comes from `pgpkeys.git` ONLY — NEVER a keyserver.** A stale keyserver copy of Greg's
key lacked his 2026-05 re-signatures and showed 2011 SHA-1 material; the R2 audit reproduced exactly
that trap. To re-vendor:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/docs/kernel/pgpkeys.git   # then: git checkout ebb799f8
export GNUPGHOME=$(mktemp -d)
gpg --import pgpkeys/keys/38DBBDC86092693E.asc pgpkeys/keys/DEA66FF797772CDC.asc
# Greg (three live UIDs); Sasha (one live UID):
gpg --export-options export-minimal,no-export-attributes \
    --export-filter 'keep-uid=mbox=greg@kroah.com || mbox=gregkh@kernel.org || mbox=gregkh@linuxfoundation.org' \
    --export-filter 'drop-subkey=usage=e' --armor --export 647F28654894E3BD457199BE38DBBDC86092693E
gpg --export-options export-minimal,no-export-attributes \
    --export-filter 'keep-uid=mbox=sashal@kernel.org' \
    --export-filter 'drop-subkey=usage=e' --armor --export E27E5D8A3403A2EF66873BBCDEA66FF797772CDC
```

Byte-reproducible **within the pinned toolchain only** (`export-minimal` semantics drift across gpg
versions — dev.gnupg.org T7990); a toolchain bump is a re-derive + re-pin review event.

## `gen/` — the throwaway differential corpus

Generated by `gen.sh` (dev-host only, gpg 2.4.x). **Regenerating produces a FRESH corpus** — the keys
are randomly generated, so key fingerprints change every run. Tests therefore read the per-run key
fingerprints + the timestamps from `gen/MANIFEST.toml`, never hardcode them. Creation times are
stamped at a fixed `gen_time` via `--faked-system-time` (so the corpus is stable-in-shape and a single
`fixture_now` sits after all of them); the corpus is evaluated at `fixture_now` (`= METADATA.fixture_now`).

Shapes (both signing-key shapes):
- `key_a.asc` — RSA-4096 **primary-signs** `[SC]`, no signing subkey (the real kernel-dev shape).
- `key_b.asc` — RSA-4096 primary **+ a signing subkey** (the chain shape; Component C / future signers).
- `key_c.asc` — a second `[SC]` signer (the "foreign / unpinned" negative).
- `key_d.asc` — **adversarial**: an **expired** signing subkey (full export, not §5.0-minimal — on
  gpg 2.4.9 `export-minimal` strips expired subkeys, T7990; we keep it so the parser+policy see it).
- `key_e.asc` — **adversarial**: a **revoked** signing subkey (0x28 revocation + binding preserved).
- `sig_<a|b>_<payload>_<sha256|sha512>.asc` — detached armored sigs over
  `payload_{empty,1b,1kib,5mib}.bin`, by key_a (primary) and key_b (subkey).
- `sig_a_1b_sha256_leadingzero.sig` — a sig whose integer `s` needs left-padding to the modulus width
  (bits ≤ 4088; pins the §6.4 left-pad-to-k requirement).
- `sig_a_1b_sha1_weak.asc` — a SHA-1 data sig (the `WeakHash(2)` negative).

No secret-key material is ever exported; the throwaway keys live only in `gen.sh`'s ephemeral,
loopback-pinentry `GNUPGHOME`, killed + removed on exit (no interactive prompt, no operator keyring
touched).
